_about: Seed data for the backend: low / medium / high flows per run, mostly read from each run's BC Whitewater description. The app reads river_runs/{id}.flowRanges from Firestore; push these there with: python3 scripts/sync_run_data.py --apply. Each number is where that level starts. 'unit' is cms (discharge) or m (water level). 'station' is the gauge the numbers are read on; 'gauge' describes one that isn't online.

ashlu-creek-bottom-mile.gauge: the online gauge below the Ashlu dam
ashlu-creek-bottom-mile.note: Usually a flow of 6 to 10 cms on the online gauge is good to go.

ashlu-creek-box-canyon.gauge: the online gauge below the Ashlu dam
ashlu-creek-box-canyon.note: 0.5 m on the staff gauge is low and 0.75 m is high, about 16 to 32 cms on the online gauge.

ashlu-creek-mine-run.gauge: the Innergex gauge below the Ashlu dam
ashlu-creek-mine-run.note: 5 to 10 cms on that gauge is medium to medium high; 20+ cms is high water. If the Elaho is below 100 cms the Mine is probably low.

ashlu-mini-mine.gauge: the online gauge below the Ashlu dam
ashlu-mini-mine.note: Run as low as 7 cms, 25 cms is a good flow; up to 90 cms it becomes solid class 4+.

big-silver-creek-middle.note: Releases of 15 cms seem like a good flow.

birkenhead-river-lower.note: Run as low as 12, 20 to 25 is low enough for most, above 35 is medium and above 50 it becomes very pushy.

boston-bar-creek.note: A good target flow is 15 cms on Coquihalla River below Needle Creek.

bridge-river.gauge: the combined Bridge and Yalakom flow
bridge-river.note: 18 cms combined felt like a nice low flow; above 25 cms some parts get demanding.

bridge-river-terzaghi-dam-to-yalakom.note: Possible with at least 10 cms from the dam; traditionally run at 50 to 90 cms releases.

callaghan-creek.gauge: the staff gauge at the take out
callaghan-creek.note: 0.1 is low, 0.3 is medium and anything over 0.5 is high.

capilano-river.note: About 3 on the stick (30 to 40 cms) is the recommended minimum; around 150 cms it gets a big water feel, and 300+ cms is no joke.

cheakamus-paradise-valley.note: Low: 25 cms, Medium: 50 cms, High: 100 cms.

cheakamus-river-balls-to-the-wall.note: Low water is 2.1 m, and the upper limit is whatever you're comfortable with.

cheakamus-river-cheakamus-lake-down.note: Similar to the Upper Cheak: minimum 2.1, medium 2.5, and high up to 3.0.

cheakamus-river-daisy-lake-canyon.note: Look for 2.3 for a nice medium level when the Callaghan is low; probably fine as low as 2.0.

cheakamus-river-upper.note: A fair minimum is 2.1, where the river is rocky and not pushy. It starts getting prime at 2.5.

chehalis-river-lower-aka-statlu-chehalis.note: Run at 9.08 m (~15 cms); 9.5 m (~35 cms) is a better low-medium; above 10 m (~90 cms) it's big water class IV; near 11 m (~300 cms) it's in flood.

chehalis-river-upper.note: 9.7 m is a recommended medium; 9.3 m was more manageable; 10.0 m was medium-high.

chilliwack-canyon-camp-foley-to-slesse.note: Low: 1.2 m (30 cms). Medium: 1.5 m (50 cms). High: 1.7 to 2 m (70 cms).

chilliwack-river-pointa-vista-to-vedder-.note: Low: 1.1 m. Medium: 1.4 m. High: 1.7 m.

chilliwack-river-post-creek-to-camp-fole.note: High: 2 m, medium: 1.6 m, low: 1.3 m.

chilliwack-river-slesse-to-tamihi.note: Low: 1.1 m. Medium: 1.4 m. High: 1.7 m.

chilliwack-river-tamihi-to-pointa-vista.note: Low: 1.1 m. Medium: 1.4 m. High: 1.7 m.

clendinning-creek.note: 60 to 70 cms on the Elaho is minimal; 80 to 150 cms is the optimal medium range; it's unreasonable much above 200 cms.

coquitlam.note: Look for levels above 20 cms; 50 to 70 cms is high.

dipper-creek.note: The Squamish gauge is far downstream; under 80 cms seems to be acceptable.

elaho-river-fear-canyon.note: 20 to 40 cms is a fun class III-IV jaunt; at 80 to 100 cms it feels like a big river; 150 cms is pushy big water IV-V; over 200 cms is terrifying in spots.

elaho-squamish.note: Low: Elaho 60 cms. Medium: Elaho 150 cms. High: Elaho 300 cms.

fraser-river-alexandra-bridge-to-yale.note: Paddled between 700 and 1,300 cms; June and July average 7,000 cms.

hurley-river-canyon.note: 10 cms gave a medium-low level, probably a good minimum. 14 to 15 is a good medium flow.

lillooet-river-between-the-lakes.note: Good flows start at 50 cms; late summer flows are around 250 cms, boily at high water.

lynn-creek.note: Too low below 14, low 14 to 20, medium 20 to 30, high 30 to 60.

mamquam-river-upper.note: 45 to 55 cms is a nice low or medium-low level.

meager-creek-lower.note: 200 cms on the Lillooet near Pemberton in July was a nice padded medium.

nahatlatch-river-canyon.note: The Vancouver Whitewater Club seem to prefer the 40 to 80 cms range.

rutherford-creek.note: 20 cms in the river below the dam is medium.

ryan-river-lower.note: Low but good to go between 30 and 40 cms, medium between 40 and 50 cms, and high anything above that.

ryan-river-upper.note: About 100 cms on the Lillooet gauge gave a medium to medium-high level.

seymour-river-canyon.note: Medium is 3 on the rock and over 4.5 is high. Online flows of 15 to 45 cms roughly match 2.5 to 5 on the rock.

seymour-river-upper-run.note: Low 30 to 50 cms, Medium 50 to 80 cms, High 80 cms+.

skagit-river-wilderness-section.note: 40 cms is a medium high flow; probably runnable down to 15 cms.

skookum-creek.note: 8 to 15 cms is a good starting point, with 8 quite low and 15 higher than most would want.

slesse-creek.note: Check the Chilliwack (at Slesse) gauge; 1.5 is a good medium level.

snowcap-creek.note: A nice medium flow when the Cheak was at about 2.40 to 2.45.

tamihi-creek-upper.note: Look for over 1.3 m and below 1.8 m on Chilliwack River above Slesse Creek, around 1.5 m.

thompson-river-goldpan-to-frog.note: Low: 300 cms, Medium: 500 cms, High: 800 cms.

upper-callaghan.note: Run from 0.1 to 0.5 m for a friendly level; above 0.5 m it gets tricky to stop and inspect the falls.

upper-tulameen.note: 8 cms is a bare minimum, 15 to 20 cms medium, and 30 cms pretty high.
